terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable object-space terms and admitted-view evidence refs.

referenceCamera.note: Three orthographic-like views constrain the exterior; clockwork, bell springs and shell thickness remain inferred.

objectClass.notes: Front, side and back views establish the exterior identity. Hidden clockwork and exact rear power geometry are explicitly inferred.

reasoning: Circular shell, concentric dial layers, twelve ticks, two bells, two hammers, two feet, two rear knobs and resettable powered motion require a compound hierarchy.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Paired and radial systems must stay separable and reviewable from front, side, back and orbit views.

details.description: Round pink body shell with shallow side depth.
Transparent dial cover above the ivory face.
Independent hour and minute hands on a central cap.
Two cream bell domes with flattened lower openings.
Dark under-bell cavities and raised lower lips.
Two separate support posts beneath the bells.
Two opposed bell hammers with cream caps.
Arched carry handle joining the upper sides.
Rear circular service plate and concentric seam.
Two rear winding knobs on independent rotary pivots.
Pink dial backlight becomes legible under power.
Narrow side profile preserves shell, bell and foot projection.
Rear-lower power inlet is provided for appliance interaction.

definitionOfDone: The three admitted views preserve round case, narrow depth, paired bells, arched handle, feet and rear service layout.
Dial, hands, bells, hammers, controls, feet and rear hardware remain named and separable.
A 5.2 second powered cue rotates hands and knobs, rings opposed hammers, moves the alarm lever, lights the dial and restores exact idle state.

proceduralStrategy: Lock the circular case, bell spacing, handle height and shallow side depth first.
Build dial, cover, ticks, hands, bells, supports, hammers, feet, lever and rear controls as named components.
Use radial repetition for twelve ticks and mirrored repetition for paired exterior systems.
Animate only named pivots and material emission, with deterministic stop reset.
Reuse primitive geometry families and avoid per-frame allocations.
assumptions: Internal escapement, gear train, bell springs and battery compartment are hidden and omitted.
Rear power inlet profile and exact shaft depth are inferred from the project connection convention.
Bell hammer attachment depth and shell wall thickness are conservative procedural estimates.
Reference artwork is stylized; material parameters reproduce SAKURA toon response rather than claiming measured physical values.
